correctness.rationale: For S>0, Parseval gives mean one for u=|F|²/S and coefficient Cauchy–Schwarz gives 0<=u<=k. Applying orthogonality again to |F|² gives E u²=1+sum_{d≠1}|R_d|²/S². Summing the difference-fiber Cauchy deficits counts each ordered off-diagonal pair once, yielding C4=1+λ(1−1/k) and the claimed exact amplitude/fiber decomposition. With s=p/2 and f(t)=t^s, the tangent remainder divided by (t−a)² is the integral of (1−r)f''(a+r(t−a)) over r in [0,1]. For s>2 this integral is strictly increasing in t on [0,k], including at 0 because 0<a<k; its value at k is A_s. This gives the quadratic majorant with contact exactly at a,k, and s=2 is exact everywhere. The proposed two-level law has mean one and second moment C4 by k(k−1)=λ(v−1), proving the normalized moment constant. A character-phase vector attains it since its squared character sum is k² at the peak and k−λ elsewhere. For s>2, contact and mean force exactly one peak, and Cauchy–Schwarz at the peak forces the character-phase vector. Distinct peaks produce distinct projective rays; no rigidity at s=2 is implied. For s=3 the quadratic remainder is (t−a)²(k−t), with quadratic coefficient k+2a, so the sixth deficit has exactly the three stated nonnegative terms. Zero coefficients contribute trivial equality. Replaying C6=(k³+(v−1)a³)/v with a=2/3,3/4,3/5 yields 37/9,85/16,289/25 for the three cited cyclic sets. value.rationale: Sharp synthesis norms are natural, and the calculations are useful as an exposition of a classical moment extremum. As a new finding, however, the exact all-p law is mechanically supplied by that extremum and the prior fourth moment, and peak rigidity is immediate from its equality profile. The only proposed extra sixth-order structure is the expansion of one cubic polynomial added to the known fourth deficit. No further quantitative stability conclusion, new inequality, or independently useful nonmechanical remainder is proved. No repair is justified.
